question.text:
• p = "Jones told the truth."
  • q = "The butler did it."
  • r = "I'll eat my hat." 
  • s = "The moon is made of green cheese."
  • t = "If water is heated to 100°C, it turns to vapor."

"If the butler did it, then either Jones told the truth or the moon is made of green cheese, but not both."

Which of the following are correct representations? (Select all that apply)

A. q → (p ⊕ s)

B. q → ((p ∨ s) ∧ ¬(p ∧ s))

C. q → (p ∨ s)

D. q → ¬(p ↔ s)
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
• p = "Jill plays basketball"
  • q = "Jim plays soccer"

Which of the following is the correct English interpretation of the proposition p ↔ q ?

A. If Jill plays basketball, then Jim plays soccer

B. Jill plays basketball if and only if Jim plays soccer

C. Jill plays basketball or Jim plays soccer, but not both

D. If Jim plays soccer, then Jill plays basketball

question.text:
• p = "Jill plays basketball"
  • q = "Jim plays soccer"

Which of the following propositions correctly capture the meaning: "Jill does not play basketball, but Jim plays soccer" ?

(Select all that apply)

A. ¬p ∧ q

B. ¬(p ∨ ¬q)

C. ¬p ∧ ¬¬q

D. q ∧ ¬p

E. ¬(p → ¬q)
